curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: appreciate the importance of well-formed letters in written communication.

interactions.prompt: Which writing is easiest for a friend to read?
choices: c a t — letters scattered far apart
cat — letters written over one another
interactions.feedback: Yes! Well-formed letters make words easy to read.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the word with clear letters in one neat group.

interactions.prompt: Put the steps for neat lowercase writing in order.
items: Start each letter in the right place
answer: Start each letter in the right place
interactions.retryHint: Prepare first, form each letter, then continue across the line.

interactions.prompt: Which letter is well formed as a lowercase a?
choices: a — closed round body with a short stem
interactions.answer: a — closed round body with a short stem
interactions.feedback: Correct! Its parts help readers recognise a.
interactions.retryHint: Look for the round body and short stem.

interactions.prompt: Match each writing habit to its benefit.
interactions.retryHint: Think about what helps a reader understand.

interactions.prompt: Your class label says bag, but the b looks like l. What is the best improvement?
choices: Rewrite b with its clear stem and round part
Erase the whole message and leave it blank
interactions.answer: Rewrite b with its clear stem and round part
interactions.feedback: Exactly! Correct letter shapes protect the meaning.
interactions.retryHint: Fix the unclear letter so the word still says bag.

choices: They help people read and understand our writing
They make writing take more space
interactions.answer: They help people read and understand our writing
interactions.retryHint: Think about the person who will read your words.
